intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the gene encoding the neurofilament light chain polypeptide (NEFL; 162280) on chromosome 8p21.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the NEFL gene, which encodes the neurofilament light chain polypeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.
checks.explanation: The abstract says NEFL mutations cause CMT, including dominant and de novo cases, but it never names CMT1F or states that the mutations are heterozygous.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NEFL gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous nonsense mutation, Glu140Stop, in one other patient.
checks.explanation: One patient with a homozygous nonsense mutation; CMT1F designation not used and the recessive causation is described as 'probably'.

checks.claim: The NEFL gene is located on chromosome 8p21.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the NEFL gene were recently reported as a cause for autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2E (CMT2E) linked to chromosome 8p21.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the 8p21 location.

paragraphs.text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is a hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy caused by mutation in the NEFL gene. It usually starts early and can be severe. Patients have distal muscle weakness and atrophy, distal sensory loss, and foot deformities. Nerve conduction velocities are reduced, in some patients into the demyelinating range. Mutations in NEFL also cause an axonal form of CMT, CMT2E, and the two forms overlap.

checks.claim: CMT1F is a hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy caused by mutation in the NEFL gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the neurofilament light chain gene (NEFL) cause early onset severe Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract says NEFL mutations cause CMT, but the designation CMT1F is not used.

checks.claim: CMT1F usually has early onset.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states early onset.

checks.claim: CMT1F can be severe.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the phenotype is often severe.

checks.claim: Patients with CMT1F have distal muscle weakness and atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: slowly progressive atrophy and weakness in distal muscles of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus
checks.explanation: Distal weakness and atrophy are described in the affected children.

checks.claim: Patients with CMT1F have distal sensory loss.
checks.evidence_quote: All have moderate sensory impairment in glove and stocking pattern.
checks.explanation: Glove-and-stocking sensory impairment is distal sensory loss.

checks.claim: Patients with CMT1F have foot deformities.
checks.evidence_quote: slowly progressive atrophy and weakness in distal muscles of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus
checks.explanation: Pes cavus is a foot deformity.

checks.claim: Nerve conduction velocities are reduced in patients with CMT1F.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that nerve conduction velocities are slowed.

checks.claim: In some patients with CMT1F, nerve conduction velocities are reduced into the demyelinating range.
checks.evidence_quote: As predicted, the reduced axonal caliber results in markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities well into the “demyelinating range”.
checks.explanation: The paper states the NCVs fall in the demyelinating range.

checks.claim: Mutations in NEFL also cause an axonal form of CMT, CMT2E.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the NEFL gene were recently reported as a cause for autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2E (CMT2E) linked to chromosome 8p21.
checks.explanation: The abstract says NEFL causes CMT2E but does not explicitly call CMT2E axonal.

checks.claim: CMT1F and CMT2E overlap.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not say CMT1F and CMT2E overlap. CMT1F is not mentioned.

paragraphs.text: Jordanova et al. (2003) screened a large series of patients with CMT for NEFL mutations. Patients with NEFL mutations had early-onset, often severe disease. Motor nerve conduction velocities were reduced, in some cases to values in the demyelinating range. This finding supported classifying some NEFL-related neuropathy as demyelinating CMT1.

checks.claim: Jordanova et al. (2003) screened a large series of patients with CMT for NEFL mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: we screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies.
checks.explanation: 323 patients counts as a large series.

checks.claim: In Jordanova et al. (2003), patients with NEFL mutations had early-onset disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states early onset.

checks.claim: In Jordanova et al. (2003), patients with NEFL mutations often had severe disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the disease was often severe.

checks.claim: In Jordanova et al. (2003), patients with NEFL mutations had reduced motor nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports slowed conduction velocities but does not say they were motor.

checks.claim: In Jordanova et al. (2003), some patients with NEFL mutations had motor nerve conduction velocities in the demyelinating range.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.
checks.explanation: The abstract says 'severely slowed' but does not mention the demyelinating range.

checks.claim: The reduced, demyelinating-range nerve conduction velocities reported by Jordanova et al. (2003) supported classifying some NEFL-related neuropathy as demyelinating CMT1.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not discuss classifying NEFL-related neuropathy as CMT1.

paragraphs.text: Most reported NEFL mutations causing CMT1F are heterozygous and show autosomal dominant inheritance or arise de novo. Autosomal recessive inheritance has been reported in families with homozygous loss-of-function (nonsense) mutations in NEFL.

checks.claim: Most reported NEFL mutations causing CMT1F are heterozygous.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected four heterozygous missense mutations--Pro8Leu, Glu90Lys, Asn98Ser and Glu396Lys--in five unrelated patients and a homozygous nonsense mutation, Glu140Stop, in one other patient.
checks.explanation: Most mutations in this cohort were heterozygous, but the abstract makes no general statement about the mutations reported in the literature.

checks.claim: Most reported heterozygous NEFL mutations causing CMT1F show autosomal dominant inheritance or arise de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: we also suggest that NEFL mutations need to be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions dominant inheritance and a de novo mutation, but not zygosity, CMT1F, or that this describes most mutations.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive inheritance of NEFL-related CMT1F has been reported in families with homozygous loss-of-function (nonsense) mutations in NEFL.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first report of a homozygous nonsense mutation of NEFL. Results of our study show that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype
checks.explanation: Based on a single patient, not families, and the recessive inheritance is described as 'probably'.

paragraphs.text: NEFL mutations also cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E (CMT2E). Mersiyanova et al. (2000) first reported this association in a Russian family.

checks.claim: NEFL mutations also cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E (CMT2E).
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the NEFL gene were recently reported as a cause for autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2E (CMT2E) linked to chromosome 8p21.
checks.explanation: The abstract says NEFL causes CMT2E but does not call it axonal.

checks.claim: Mersiyanova et al. (2000) first reported the association of NEFL mutations with CMT2E, in a Russian family.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract says only that NEFL mutations were 'recently reported'. It does not name Mersiyanova et al. or a Russian family.

paragraphs.text: Jordanova et al. (2003) identified heterozygous NEFL mutations in patients with early-onset CMT and reduced nerve conduction velocities. Some of these mutations arose de novo.

checks.claim: Jordanova et al. (2003) identified heterozygous NEFL mutations in patients with early-onset CMT and reduced nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein. Patients have an early onset
checks.explanation: The mutations, early onset and slowed conduction velocities are in the abstract, but heterozygosity is not stated.

checks.claim: Some of the NEFL mutations identified by Jordanova et al. (2003) arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the first nerve biopsy of a CMT patient with a de novo missense mutation in NEFL
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a de novo mutation.

paragraphs.text: Homozygous nonsense mutations in NEFL were later identified in patients with an autosomal recessive, early-onset, severe form of NEFL-related CMT.

checks.claim: Homozygous nonsense mutations in NEFL were identified in patients with an autosomal recessive form of NEFL-related CMT.
checks.evidence_quote: All four affected children were homozygous for a nonsense mutation at glutamate 210 (E210X) in the NEFL gene; both parents were heterozygous carriers.
checks.explanation: A homozygous nonsense mutation was found in a family with autosomal recessive CMT.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive NEFL-related CMT caused by homozygous nonsense mutations is early-onset and severe.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first demonstration of a recessive NEFL mutation, which appears to cause a simple loss of function, resulting in a severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy with unique features.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disease as severe and early-onset.

references.label: Jordanova et al. (2003)
